clue.text: Ethicist loosely associated with people of faith

indicators.note: something held loosely is not fixed in place

blocks.note: the fodder, a moral philosopher, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A moral philosopher is said to have vague links with religious believers.
explanation.walkthrough: ETHICIST and THEISTIC use exactly the same eight letters, and the surface makes 'loosely associated' read as one phrase when the split falls between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Theistic describes belief in a god, the outlook shared by religious believers.

clue.text: Sting ultimately got to perform like Eminem?

blocks.note: the last letter of goT
Eminem is a rapper, so performing like him is rapping

explanation.surface: The singer Sting apparently gets to perform in the style of the rapper Eminem.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting the musician sits happily beside Eminem, but here the word is a police sting, an operation set up to catch someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a covert police operation designed to catch criminals, which is a kind of snare.

clue.text: Impressive photograph online?

blocks.note: E- is the prefix for electronic or online things, as in email
pic is short for picture

explanation.walkthrough: The online prefix comes first even though 'online' is printed last: an e-pic would be a photo posted on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic in modern slang means grand or awesome, on a heroic scale.

clue.text: Possibly how that woman will get hold of Ray's winkle?

blocks.note: 'that woman' is she, and 'she will' contracts to she'll
a ray is a flatfish, so to catch one you would fish

explanation.surface: A woman plans to grab something belonging to a man called Ray, with a cheeky double meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a man's name and the surface turns smutty, but a ray is the flat sea fish; the apostrophe just keeps the sentence grammatical. 'Possibly' flags the playful whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A winkle is a small sea snail in a hard coiled case, eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Warning assumes this setter would menace

blocks.note: an intimation is a hint or advance notice
the setter speaks as I, and 'I would' contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A warning takes it for granted that the compiler would threaten someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Menace' reads as a verb after 'would', but it is the noun: the definition has to match a noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimidation is the act of frightening someone with threats, which is what a menace amounts to.

clue.text: Pressure games beset by wrong'un selected for England?

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded

blocks.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a bad lot
P is the symbol for pressure in physics
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: high-pressure matches troubled by a wrong'un, a googly, from a bowler picked for England.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wrong'un is a googly, which suits the England surface; here it is a rotter. A player is capped when given a cap for playing for their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capped means receiving a cap to mark playing in a national team, so it amounts to international selection.

clue.text: Following a brief threesome, Penny just got out of bed

indicators.note: a brief thing is cut short

blocks.note: used as printed
a trio, cut short by its last letter
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A racy scene: after a quick three-in-a-bed, a woman named Penny has just risen.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is the seabed. Atrip is a nautical term for an anchor just lifted clear of the bottom, so the bedroom surface hides a ship weighing anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call an anchor atrip at the moment it is pulled free of the seabed floor.

clue.text: Inscrutable Roger Federer initially served a winner against Potter earlier

blocks.note: to potter about is to poke about, doing nothing much
the initials of the tennis player
a serve the opponent cannot touch is an ace, so the server aced

explanation.surface: Federer, famously calm, serves an ace against an opponent called Potter.
explanation.walkthrough: Potter looks like a surname, the opponent; it is the verb, and 'earlier' moves it to the front. 'Against' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a deadpan face showing no feeling, like a card player hiding a hand, is impossible to read.

clue.text: Yesterday was one of his number essentially held back?

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre

blocks.note: the Irish ballad is a much-sung number
the middle two letters of hELd

explanation.surface: Yesterday, the Beatles song, is called one of someone's numbers, held back from release.
explanation.walkthrough: Yesterday is also the 2019 film about a world that forgets the Beatles, directed by Danny Boyle. 'Number' flips from the song in the surface to a different song, Danny Boy.
explanation.definitionFit: The British director made the 2019 comedy film named after the Beatles hit, so that movie is among his works.

clue.text: Sustains complaints one left on the counter

blocks.note: ailments are illnesses, things you complain of
one is I and left is L, naming the pair already standing side by side inside the complaints word

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper bears grumbles about something someone left on the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The I and L that already sit side by side in AILMENTS are turned round, giving ALIMENTS. 'Counter' suggests a shop but means contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: To aliment is an old verb for to feed or provide nourishment, keeping someone alive.

clue.text: Dejected British monkey peeled bananas

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for British
mONKEy without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sad monkey in Britain has been peeling bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the monkey's food, but it is the instruction to rearrange, meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone broken is crushed in spirit, overwhelmed by sorrow or defeat.

clue.text: A flat for one in Turkey taking ages being renovated

indicators.note: a renovated place is rebuilt

blocks.note: fodder taken letter for letter
more fodder, added on by 'taking'

explanation.surface: An apartment in Turkey is taking forever to be done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A flat' reads as an apartment, which the renovation surface encourages; it is the musical flat. A single flat at the start of the stave is one example of a key signature.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the sharps or flats written at the start of each staff show the key, and one flat is such a marking.

clue.text: Italian man wanting to separate welcomed by foxy girls sleeping around

indicators.note: a guest welcomed in is inside

blocks.note: foxy means cunning
Umberto, an Italian name, without its final 'to'
to part is to separate

explanation.surface: An Italian man wants to break up with a pair of sexy women who are sleeping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping around' suggests promiscuity; in the definition it just means girls asleep in a group. 'Foxy' looks like the girls' description and is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepover where a group of friends, usually children, spend the night together at one house.

clue.text: Eclipse lovers had own blankets

indicators.note: a blanket covers what lies under it

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of the first word to the second-last of the last

explanation.surface: Two lovers watching a solar eclipse each brought their own blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blankets' looks like the lovers' belongings; it is the verb, to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse someone is to outshine them and make them seem less important.

clue.text: Fine leg strides to the crowd in Melbourne Cricket Ground

blocks.note: surface reading: a fielding position in cricket, behind the batsman on the leg side

blocks.clueFragment: strides to the crowd in Melbourne Cricket Ground
blocks.note: setter's reading: 'strides' is Australian slang for trousers, so these are trousers with fine, narrow legs

explanation.surface: A fielder at fine leg walks towards the spectators at the great Melbourne cricket stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine leg' and 'strides' read as a cricketer on the move. To an Australian crowd, strides are trousers, so fine-leg strides are skinny trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainpipes are very narrow tight trousers, named after their resemblance to thin tubes, popular with Teddy boys.

clue.text: Barman withdrawing milder bevvy periodically

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the kept letters run backwards

blocks.note: the even letters of mIlDeR bEvVy

explanation.surface: A bartender stops serving a weaker drink every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: A barman here is someone who writes bars of music, a composer; Giuseppe Verdi wrote operas such as Aida. A bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian opera composer wrote music, which is set out in measures, making him a crossword-only sense of barman.

clue.text: Outlaw recalled venture controlled by short tyrant

indicators.note: a short version is cut down
something recalled is called back

blocks.note: a despot, minus its last letter
to venture is to dare

explanation.surface: A criminal remembers a scheme run by a diminutive dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short tyrant' can make you think of Napoleon; it is simply the word for a tyrant with its tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless bandit of the Wild West, someone living beyond the law.

clue.text: Egg on your face having gone into prison

indicators.note: going into a place puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to encage is to lock up
yOUR with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: Being caught and jailed leaves you with egg on your face, humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'egg on your face' is the whole surface idiom, but the definition stops after 'on'. 'Prison' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them forward, spurring them into action.

clue.text: Wealthy male taking ecstasy in German house

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it

blocks.note: a straight synonym
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a stag is a male deer, and a men-only party

explanation.surface: A rich man takes drugs at a house in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wealthy male' reads as one person, but it splits into two pieces, and the drug goes into the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The building in Berlin houses the national parliament, and a parliament chamber is also called a house.

clue.text: Caught fish with this? Or in this?

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
an angler winds the line on a reel

explanation.surface: A riddle about fishing: is the catch made with this, or kept in it?
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves pretend to be the definition. The first half is wordplay, a reel being what you fish with; the answer is what fish go in once caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket that an angler carries to hold the day's catch.

clue.text: Large animal in river sinks carrying naked person over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped

blocks.note: in and hip both mean fashionable
the Po is Italy's longest river
in snooker to sink a ball is to pot it
hUMAn stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A big beast in a river goes under carrying a naked swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In river' looks like the animal's habitat, but 'in' is a piece of its own, meaning trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: The African river horse is one of the heaviest land mammals, a huge beast.

clue.text: This beast needs power to make sudden attack

blocks.note: a pounce is a sudden spring on prey
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A wild animal has to summon strength before it can spring on its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the answer plus the power letter makes the attack, so take that letter away from the attack to find the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Unspecified number dropping from extreme pain held up exercise practice

indicators.note: what drops out of something leaves it
in a down clue, raising the letters up makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: agony is severe suffering
n in maths stands for any number

explanation.surface: Some people drop out of a painful exercise class they had kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: N comes out of AGONY, and the four letters left are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a discipline of stretching poses and breathing, done as physical training and meditation.

clue.text: Picked up light meal and a number of bits

indicators.note: a sound picked up is heard

blocks.note: a bite is a quick snack

explanation.surface: Someone collects a snack along with a handful of odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits' looks like scraps of food; it is computing bits.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, eight binary digits make up one unit of data storage.

clue.text: Bolt in trouble taking performance enhancing drugs?

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

blocks.note: to dog someone is to trouble them persistently
a pin is a bolt or peg

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, the sprinter, in trouble for using banned drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt looks like the Jamaican sprinter; it is a metal fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Doping is the use of banned stimulants or steroids by athletes to gain an edge.

clue.text: Trivial piece repulsed a politician

indicators.note: something repulsed is driven back

blocks.note: a piece is slang for a gun
used as printed
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A politician finds some small item or article disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repulsed' reads as disgusted, but it means pushed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or importance, worthless and ineffective.

clue.text: High priest on television was out of order

indicators.note: the two pieces are not placed in the sequence they are printed, so 'was' goes first

blocks.note: used as printed
Father Ted is the priest in the Irish TV sitcom

explanation.surface: A senior cleric on TV behaved badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High priest' reads as one title, but 'High' is the definition alone. Father Ted is a 1990s sitcom about three priests on an Irish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for heavily intoxicated by drink or drugs, just as high is.

clue.text: Teenager goes off to evolve

indicators.note: something going off turns bad or explodes

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A teenager storms off in order to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: TEENAGER and GENERATE share all eight letters; the surface makes 'goes off' a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to produce or develop something, bringing it into being over time.
